newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer buys stores from Littlewoods.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer buys stores from Littlewoods.

text.p: Britain's biggest clothing retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Thursday it was buying 19 stores from Littlewoods for 192.5 million pounds ($322.8 million) cash.
"This is a very good deal for Marks & Spencer, which will enhance shareholder value," chairman Sir Richard Greenbury told the group's annual general meeting.

"This outstanding opportunity gives us an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres, which again underlines our confidence in the future of the high street," he said in a statement.
The group expects to start fitting out the stores next February and intends to begin opening them progressively through the year.

Littlewoods, the privately-owned retail-to-football pools group, last month abandoned plans to sell its entire 135 high-street stores, saying it would instead refocus strategy while selling off selected sites. Littlewoods, owned by the secretive millionaire Moores family, put its retail chain up for sale in March.
Marks and Spencer also said that its clothing sales in the UK in the first quarter of the current financial year were up by nearly 10 percent, while foods sales grew by 2.3 percent.
It said that the strength of sterling would reduce its profits for the year by 20 million pounds but that lower UK corporation tax would improve its net profits by the same amount.
Shares in the group were up 6-1/2 pence at 593-1/2 at 1045 GMT.
